reason: The Commission reports that full accession to the Common Transit Convention followed in November 2025 and that the interoperability of customs operations was significantly enhanced, and it records NCTS Phase 6 connected to the common transit network. This is an independent EU finding of an effect beyond the system's launch.

The Commission links the Convention accession and interoperability directly to the rollout of the transit system, which is the technical condition for connecting to the common transit network. Accession also needed legal and other technical steps, so the system was a necessary contributor rather than the only cause.

The claim of better social protection for Moldovans working abroad comes from the Government alone, and no item among the 59 Moldova items on this issue measures coverage or benefits paid under the agreements. Signing and entry into force are not success.
The Government asserts the effect of its own agreements without data, so contribution cannot be confirmed beyond the general purpose of coordination agreements.

The statement of substantial progress towards a resilient cyber ecosystem is the Government's own; the Commission confirms the EU donation of equipment and licences and an operational Agency and CERT, but not the wider resilience the Government claims.
Several donors supported the Agency in the same period, including EUPM, TAIEX, Sweden, the OSCE and Estonia, so the share due to this project cannot be separated on the Government's statement alone.
